paragraphs: Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Ami.

Hyman calls him a colleague of Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, citing Ketubot 85a. Mareimar or Rav Yeimar came to his public lecture, as in Pesachim 100a. Rav Ashi called him “Master” and asked him a question, as in Zevachim 7b.

He is also mentioned, Hyman says, in Pesachim 21a [a matching passage is in Pesachim 61a], asserting that a change of a sacrifice’s beneficiary DOES apply after death; in Zevachim 4a [a matching passage is in Zevachim 4b], likewise concerning a change of beneficiary; and in Chullin 82a, concerning the heifer whose neck is broken.

notes.text: Ketubot 85a explicitly names Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, not Rabbah. Zevachim 7b matches the posthumous sacrificial-beneficiary discussion; the supplied Pesachim 21a citation remains a source question.

The saved whole Davidson Pesachim 61a scalar names Rav Pinchas son of Rav Ami on a change of sacrificial beneficiary after death. The saved whole Zevachim 4b scalar instead names Rav Pinchas son of Rav Mari. Both matching locators are added beside supplied Pesachim 21a and Zevachim 4a; Ami/Mari is not harmonized and no print-error mechanism is claimed. The earlier Ketubot comparison supporting Huna rather than Rabbah is inherited, not newly inspected. The colleague relationship remains Hyman’s characterization, and full supplied Rav titles are preserved.

Hyman’s printed article crosses pp. 1012–1013. It gives Pesachim 21a and Zevachim 4a. At the matching Pesachim 61a the speaker is Rav Pinchas son of Rav Ami, and Zevachim 4b names Rav Pinchas son of Rav Mari. Ketubot 85a places Pinchas in the same episode as Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Pesachim 100a preserves Mareimar or Rav Yeimar as alternative reporters. In Zevachim 7b Rav Ashi addresses Pinchas as mar and asks about the consequences of his position. Pinchas affirms it. In Chullin 82a Pinchas attributes the statement about the heifer to Reish Lakish, Rav Ashi objects, and the discussion ends with R’ Chiyya bar Abba reporting it in R’ Yochanan’s name.
